subject: AWS Private Offer: buyer approval gates, term windows & legal signoff
messages:

Cc: AWS Marketplace PM <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer — term lengths and buyer approval gates

Neha — thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to internal approval and I need to confirm two things before I take this to procurement: 

1) Term flexibility: procurement prefers 12-month commitments but I can get 24 months if pricing is compelling. Can Redwood offer a blended rate for a 12 vs 24 month private offer?

2) Buyer approval gating: our security/compliance team requires that a specific buyer list be whitelisted for the private offer (multi-division purchase). Will AWS Marketplace private offers support per-buyer approvals or do we need separate POs per BU?

If possible, include any co-sell eligibility notes we should surface to AWS for PS and GTM credits.

Thanks —
Jared
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Platform Inc.

Subject: Re: Private Offer — term lengths and buyer approval gates

Hi Jared — great question and really glad Acme is moving this forward. High-level answers below; I'll loop in legal/partnerships for the mechanics.

Term & pricing options
- 12-month standard private offer: list price with a volume discount tier.
- 24-month committed offer: we can provide a blended effective rate (examples below) that materially lowers per-unit cost but requires a 24-month payment schedule.
- We can also structure a 12+12 renewal at a reduced introductory rate for year 1 if that helps procurement hit annual budget windows.

Buyer approval gating
- AWS private offers support buyer-level whitelists (you can submit specific AWS account IDs to the PO). For multi-BU deployments we typically ask customers to either:
  a) submit a consolidated whitelist (preferred), or
  b) create separate offers per BU if billing/commit needs to be isolated.

Co-sell eligibility
- To surface co-sell: confirm the product listing (we have a co-sell-enabled SKU) and provide AWS with a joint GTM contact for PS credits. Vanessa — can you confirm the SKU and the checklist we should provide to Jared?

If these options look OK I can put together a draft term sheet and a passable pricing grid for procurement.

Next steps:
- Vanessa to confirm co-sell checklist + SKU.
- Karthik to flag any legal requirements for a 24-month private offer.
- I will draft PO term sheet and share for review.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Marketplace Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — quick notes from the co-sell/partnership side: 

1) SKU & listing: Product is co-sell enabled; SKU RWI-PROD-001. I'll attach the Redwood_AWS_CoSell_Checklist — it covers GTM contacts, PS scoping, and the co-sell playbook items AWS asks for.

2) Approval gating practicalities:
- Consolidated whitelist of AWS account IDs is easiest for procurement and preserves single PO economics.
- If Acme needs per-BU billing isolation, we can do separate offers but expect loss of some volume-tier pricing unless aggregated by a master agreement.

3) Pricing guidance:
- 24-month blended rate typically saves ~18-22% vs 12-month in our recent deals. We can run a modeled example for Acme's usage profile if you share forecasted consumption.

Karthik — FYI for legal: for 24-month locked pricing we normally require an early-termination schedule and clear payment terms (monthly vs upfront). Jared — is Acme open to monthly invoicing against a committed usage baseline, or do you need annual billing?

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner GTM | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer — term lengths and buyer approval gates

Jared / team — legal here. A few compliance/legal items to note for structuring a 24-month private offer: 

- Term / payment: We can support monthly invoicing against a committed baseline or an annual prepay. Monthly preserves customer cash flow but requires an explicit committed minimum and an early-termination charge if Acme drops below baseline.
- Buyer whitelists: we'll need an authoritative list of AWS account IDs and a primary billing owner per account. If Acme expects to add accounts later, include a change process (email to marketplace@redwood.com and a 10-business-day window to update the PO).
- Data residency & audit: if any BU requires EU residency, that needs to be called out and may change the offer (region-specific SKUs).

I'll draft a short addendum covering early termination fees and the whitelist change process. Neha — please confirm desired billing cadence and whether Acme prefers a 12+12 renewal structure vs 24 locked.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

- 12-month PO with an optional year-2 renewal at a pre-agreed rate (12+12) — keeps our fiscal year clean.
- Consolidated whitelist for our first rollout (we'll provide the AWS account IDs by end of week).
- Monthly invoicing against a committed baseline is preferred (helps cash ops).

Next asks from Acme to Redwood: 
1) Draft private-offer term sheet reflecting the 12+12 framework and monthly invoicing.
2) Co-sell checklist + confirmation of SKU (Vanessa: thanks for the checklist).
3) DocuSign-ready PO once legal addendum is agreed.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Jared
